1_generate_alpha2_store.label: GENERATED by the app's own corpus generator (src/testing/corpus_gen.py): invented articles, not any operator's corpus. It does not stand for gate section 1c item 7.

live_corpus_in_target_form.method: distinct stored spellings in the LIVE corpus that this normaliser would rewrite to alpha2. 0 = the live corpus is already in the target form. Codes with no canonical form are not counted: they say nothing about which form the corpus uses

country_codes_block.method: every registered country column of the incoming corpus is converted to the store's canonical form (alpha2) before the value-keyed joins; a code the converter does not recognise is left unchanged and listed, and NULL stays NULL

scan.caveat: `duplicates` counts only the columns the restore normalises. A column marked normalised:false is scanned and REPORTED but excluded from the total; what a group there means differs per column, so each carries its own reason rather than one blanket claim -- an earlier single sentence said every such group was 'a question about a migration rather than about a restore', which was true of stat_figures.ref_area and false of stat_subscriptions.country, where two installs typing one country in two cases really did duplicate at restore until the merge key was folded

places.country_alpha3.reason: alpha-3 BY DESIGN (Q312 = a: a Place carries both forms from birth, for the alpha-3 display surfaces); normalising it toward the store's alpha-2 would overwrite the very form the column exists to hold. It is derived from `country` and never a join key

stat_figures.ref_area.reason: the area code AS PUBLISHED by the statistics agency, stored alpha-3 by convention (src/api/governments.py reads it back in that form) and part of uq_stat_figure_vintage -- normalising it to alpha-2 would corrupt the Governments surface and split one observation's vintages in two

stat_subscriptions.country.reason: the World Bank API's own `country` PARAMETER, replayed verbatim on the next fetch and carrying non-codes such as the literal 'all' (src/api/governments.py:614); it is part of uq_stat_subscription, so rewriting it would make a re-subscribe duplicate instead of dedupe (Q311: external contracts stay alpha-2 behind converters). EXEMPT FROM THE REWRITE, NOT FROM THE PROBLEM: the value arrives through a free-text box that folds neither case nor form, so `_merge_statistics`' subscription key compares it case-insensitively -- the comparison is merge.py's own business and rewrites nothing the World Bank will ever be sent

scan.method: per country-bearing column, the distinct stored spellings are grouped by their canonical form; a group with more than one spelling is one duplicate. Codes with no canonical form (statistical aggregates, the app's non-ISO jurisdictions, junk) are listed as unresolved, never counted either way

estimate.basis: 20000 rows of keyword_mentions.country rewritten in 0.038 s on this machine and rolled back. It leaves out the commit and the log checkpoint of a real window, so the run is usually slower

extrapolation.basis: the sweep: 4,740,060 rows in 16.3 s (290,158 rows/s) applied to 20.9 M keyword_mentions rows; the safety copy and the proof: seconds per GB measured on a 1.72 GB generated store, applied to the 11.7 GB store of 2026-07-09. An ESTIMATE, not a measurement: a larger store has deeper indexes, a spinning disk or an encrypted file is slower, and the operator's own reading under gate section 1c item 7 replaces it.
